UnitStatement: ADR-0001 records the operation-seam engine unification: the wasm32 build of operation_applier becomes the sole browser-mode engine.
ADR-0001 status is accepted, dated 2026-06-11.

The decision rests on a human project authority ruling of 2026-06-11 accepting plans/PLAN_2026-06-11_operation_seam_unification.md §2 as proposed; recorded as D-13 (state RULED) in execution/_Coordination/_DECISIONS/_REGISTER.md.
The decision cross-references DEC-020 in execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md §12.
The structured editor-operation seam is the enforcement point for no-silent-defaults, unit/dimension checks, before-state integrity, and professional-boundary receipts.
The operation seam was implemented twice (plan §1, FACT basis).
The authoritative engine is core/model_operations/operation_applier/src/lib.rs (Rust, ~4,885 lines, 34 tests), invoked by the validate_model_operation and apply_model_operation Tauri commands.
The browser mirror is apps/desktop/src/services/operationService.ts (~2,280 lines, 17 tests), used whenever no Tauri backend exists.
The browser mirror is used in Vite dev mode, all jsdom/Vitest edit-loop tests, the Playwright e2e harness, and agent in-browser smoke evidence.
The mirror was a deliberate code-level choice; its file header names the Rust crate as the contract reference.
The mirror bought real value: the browser evidence loop (Vite dev, jsdom/Vitest, Playwright) and agent verification velocity.
No executable contract enforced alignment between the two engines; each suite tests only its own engine.
No ADR recorded the decision; the ADR surface DEL-00-01 anticipated did not exist in the worktree until this entry created it.
Two scheduled work fronts multiply the duplication: the R2 from-scratch authoring set (~4-6 new operation kinds) and Phase B unit-aware fields (conversion/tolerance logic per DEC-018).
The failure mode if unresolved is environment-dependent validation outcomes and environment-dependent canonical model hashes, fracturing the no-silent-defaults and hash-evidence guarantees.
Decision: adopt the wasm32 build of core/model_operations/operation_applier as the sole browser-mode operation engine in every environment without a Tauri backend.

Decision: retire the TypeScript mirror's validation/apply logic at plan tranche T4 by deletion-by-replacement — the Rust crate compiled to WebAssembly becomes the engine everywhere before the mirror logic is removed.
Decision: TypeScript retains only the React UI, intent builders, and a thin routing adapter (Tauri present -> invoke authoritative path unchanged; otherwise -> the wasm module).
Decision: the browser evidence loop (Vitest, Playwright, agent smoke) is preserved throughout the transition and afterward exercises the shipped engine rather than a copy.
All alternatives were presented to and declined by the human project authority in the 2026-06-11 ruling (plan §1 and §2).
Declined alternative: keep dual engines plus a permanent cross-engine contract test — safe but inefficient as a steady state; Phase B unit-aware work compounds dual-maintenance cost.
Declined alternative: delete browser-mode editing outright — guts the GUI test layer and agent verification loop, forcing evidence onto nonexistent packaged-native automation weak on macOS.
Declined alternative: a local Rust dev-sidecar over HTTP — adds a process and a network surface against the local-first/no-daemon posture.
Declined alternative: deferral until T1 contract-corpus evidence — declined because scheduled R2 and Phase B work fronts multiply the duplicated surface while the decision waits.

Consequence (toolchain prerequisite): the wasm32-unknown-unknown Rust target and wasm-bindgen tooling with pinned versions become build prerequisites; build scripts fail explicitly when tooling is absent — no silent fallback.
Consequence: a wasm build step enters the frontend loop — an npm script produces the wasm artifact for the desktop app; generated artifacts are not committed.
Consequence (debugging posture): browser-mode engine issues are debugged through the engine's structured diagnostics rather than by stepping through native TypeScript engine logic.
Consequence (bundle size/startup impact): mitigated by lazy engine init, measured against the existing ~577 kB index chunk and recorded in T4 evidence.
Consequence (loading shim obligation): an explicit diagnostic when the wasm asset is absent; never a silent fallback.

Affected packages (per plan §3 write targets and run-record fan-out): PKG-16 (DEL-16-02, DEL-16-03), PKG-00 (DEL-00-01, DEL-00-02, DEL-00-08), PKG-07 (DEL-07-02), and PKG-10 (DEL-10-03, T1 rider only).

Reconsideration trigger: if wasm loading proves intractable in the test environment (Vitest/jsdom), stop and escalate to human ruling; reintroducing a TypeScript engine as a workaround is not authorized.
Reconsideration trigger: material bundle-size or startup regression beyond what lazy engine init mitigates.
Reconsideration trigger: toolchain availability drift — the wasm32 target or pinned bindgen tooling becoming unavailable or unpinnable.
